executedChecks: Source numeric constants match pinned values.
Normal case: Fighter with 1 EC spends 1 EC and 75 stamina; emits fighter-shockwave with the normal variant, width, 760 ms producer duration, offset origin, and collision-resolved endpoint.
Giant case: Fighter with 100 EC spends exactly 100 EC and emits the giant variant, width, range, and 1150 ms producer duration.
Zero EC and non-Fighter cases emit no fighter-shockwave and do not consume EC.
Effect emission occurs before wave-target search; the empty-target case needs no victim and invokes no kill processing.
Captured payload has no targetId or outcome; one-body-damage is only the variant's rule label.
Two executions of the same slash request with 2 EC create two wave emissions and consume twice; the producer has no receipt duplicate gate.
Negative cases: non-playing phase, missing sword, dead, ejected, vented, insufficient stamina, and ability, storage, or consciousness rejection emit no wave.
vmBoundaryStubs: Fighter authorization and sword ownership predicates
Ability, storage, and consciousness ensure functions
Stamina spending, guard opening, bot attack-start recording, and feedback
Collision/path resolver, configured to return a known endpoint
pushMagicEffect capture, pushSound, event/touch, and win check
victim processing throws if unexpectedly invoked
scopeLimits: This executes the extracted producer functions in Node VM; it does not establish live gameplay authorization, collision, target selection, or victim/damage outcomes.
The emitted effect call is captured at pushMagicEffect; no registered shader, GPU, browser, screen-size, playback-speed, or visual acceptance is tested.
No producer receipt-level duplicate prevention exists in this tested branch; separate host/audio duplicate launch checks are owned by the parent task.
This is static/source-bound CPU evidence only, not game integration or release acceptance.
